body.estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\mathbb E_{P_X}[\tau_P(X)_+-\pi_0(X)\tau_P(X)]\), with frontier \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)}\inf_{I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\)

sampling_model.design: One \(P\)-independent non-anticipating contextual design chooses the known propensity \(e_t^{\mathsf D}(H_{t-1},X_t)\) from observed history and the fresh context; one \(P\)-independent Borel interval map is evaluated on the resulting observed trajectory.
sampling_model.units: The contexts are independent draws from a stationary density on \([0,1]^d\); the observed reward satisfies \(Y_t=\mu_{A_t}(X_t)+\sigma\varepsilon_t\) with fresh conditionally independent standard-normal innovations.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment satisfies \(A_t\mid(H_{t-1},X_t)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_t^{\mathsf D})\), and only the selected-arm reward \(Y_t\) is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: No exogenous propensity floor is imposed; the design must generate any exploration needed for honesty while satisfying \(\sup_P\mathcal R_T(P,\mathsf D)\le\rho\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The attaining handle uses predictable local regression, polynomial approximation for the positive-part functional, and a bias-aware augmented score; all nuisance accuracy must be derived from the design-generated local counts.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1, 2, 5, and 6 give and attain a Pareto product frontier between participant regret and treatment-effect point-estimation error in a finite-armed experiment.
Theorem 5.1 gives the minimax regret exponent under the local Hölder--margin condition, and Proposition 3.1 yields \(\alpha\beta\le d\) for finite \(\alpha\).
The local asymptotic minimax result bounds regular ATE estimation under every covariate- and history-dependent assignment design.
Theorem 1 characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and Theorem 2 gives online one-step inference under a negligible rule-value remainder.
The paper derives minimax rates for nonsmooth \(L_r\)-functionals by polynomial approximation and moment-matching priors in fixed Gaussian white noise.
The lower and upper results match a CATE mean-squared-error versus regret frontier for finitely many contexts with fixed-order gaps.
The central theorem gives a studentized central limit theorem for predictably weighted augmented inverse-propensity estimators of fixed arm values.
The CADR theorem obtains asymptotic normality for a fixed contextual-policy value by conditional-variance stabilization.
Theorem 1 constructs nonasymptotic doubly robust confidence sequences for a fixed off-policy value under predictable logging policies.

The paper constructs one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare that remain valid regardless of the margin condition; uniform separation and margin behavior govern its first-order welfare--precision comparison.
The main theorem derives asymptotic normality and adaptive semiparametric efficiency for regular scalar targets under directional stability and verifies the condition for LinUCB.

Section 4.1, Theorem 1 proves stability and asymptotic normality for ordinary least squares under regularized EXP4, yielding asymptotically exact Wald intervals for fixed linear functionals; Section 4.2, Theorem 2 gives the same algorithm a near-minimax regret bound.

body.tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while a credible post-experiment claim about the gain from individualized targeting needs precisely those observations and becomes nonregular near treatment ties. A two-direction theorem identifies the gain from the observed trajectory law under positive arm exposure and constructs observationally equivalent Gaussian laws with separated gains when a benchmark-relevant arm has zero exposure. The project restricts inference to one common \(P\)-independent Borel trajectory-to-interval map, uses a local Tsybakov margin condition, verifies nonempty Hölder--margin and fixed-gap classes, converts coverage into an extended-valued scalar-functional modulus, and exposes the attaining bottleneck through a cellwise semi-infinite information-allocation primal and dual. The fixed-gap edge is \(\rho^{-1/2}\), while the complete Hölder-margin frontier requires proving or disproving implicit allocation saturation and realizing its quotas under the welfare budget. The published Perchet--Rigollet feasibility exponent supplies a cited sanity boundary; \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) serve as the mandatory early kill test.

project_justification.gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results concern point-estimation error for finite-arm treatment gaps or finitely many fixed-gap strata. Praharaj and Khamaru obtain asymptotic Wald inference for fixed linear functionals and near-minimax regret from one linear contextual-bandit design, but not uniform nonregular honest width under a hard welfare budget. Other adaptive confidence-interval results take the logging design as given and target fixed policy values. Optimal-value inference treats the tie nonregularity but does not price exploration by participant welfare. None of these results characterizes the honest expected-width envelope over both designs and common observed-trajectory interval maps.
project_justification.niche: The targeting gain \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\) joins a regular benchmark-evaluation component to a nonsmooth positive-part component. A welfare budget endogenizes the information geometry because sampling the locally inferior arm has gap-dependent cost. This creates a sequential ordered-modulus problem that is absent from both ordinary contextual regret and fixed-design functional estimation.
project_justification.fill: Positive cumulative exposure identifies the target from the observed trajectory law, whereas an explicit zero-exposure pair proves nonidentification on benchmark-relevant regions. Every reported interval is one common \(P\)-independent Borel map of the observed trajectory, and an explicit constant-gap Gaussian law verifies that both frontier domains are nonempty under mutually compatible primitive constants. The procedure-free coverage reduction makes the extended-valued sequential targeting-gain modulus the lower-bound object. Target-separating local alternative sets generate armwise conditional-Gaussian KL coefficients, a semi-infinite covering program, and a measure-valued dual; the open saturation question asks whether their implicit width level can be realized by welfare-priced predictable exploration and a bias-aware connected interval. The fixed-gap theorem anchors the compulsory branch, and the open kernel requires a matching rate with every threshold derived from primitives.

body.related_work: Simchi-Levi and Wang establish a finite-arm Pareto frontier between regret and treatment-effect point-estimation error; Theorem 5 is written as the strict honest-width strengthening relevant here. Perchet and Rigollet, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, supply the Hölder--margin minimax regret exponent and the restriction \(\alpha\beta\le d\); the supporting feasibility lemma first extends their local margin inequality by the probability bound and then uses a routine fixed-scale Gaussian translation rather than claiming an independent contribution. Hu, Kallus, and Mao supply the selective local-regression architecture. Luedtke and van der Laan locate the pathwise differentiability boundary of optimal value. Han, Jiao, and Mukherjee are cited only for nonsmooth fixed-Gaussian polynomial-approximation and moment-matching methodology, not for the adaptive regression experiment used here. Kaufmann, Cappé, and Garivier provide the allocation-agnostic sequential change of measure and the standard conditional Gaussian innovation framework, while Cai and Low provide the coverage-to-length modulus logic. Hadad and coauthors, Bibaut and coauthors, Waudby-Smith and coauthors, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, and Shen and coauthors provide adaptive score, martingale, anytime-valid, efficiency, and stability tools for regular or fixed-policy targets; they inform the upper construction but do not determine this envelope. Praharaj and Khamaru, Section 4.1, Theorem 1 and Section 4.2, Theorem 2, construct one regularized EXP4 design with asymptotically exact Wald inference for fixed linear functionals and near-minimax regret; this is informed-by prior art because pointwise linear-functional asymptotics and an unconstrained regret guarantee do not deliver uniform honest minimax width for a nonregular positive-part target under a hard welfare budget. Li, Shi, and Simchi-Levi balance regret and CATE error over finitely many contexts, whereas the present bottleneck is learning and pricing continuous small-gap regions. Ponomarev and Semenova construct one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare that remain valid regardless of the margin condition; uniform separation and margin behavior separately govern their first-order welfare--precision comparison, while two-sided budgeted adaptive width remains outside their result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exponent suggested by a regret packing is not automatically an exponent for the scalar targeting gain. Balanced sign flips can cancel in \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\), and a local design can concentrate information on precisely the cells a naive packing treats symmetrically. No local branch is part of the contribution until the alternatives in Lemma 6 are shown to belong to the class, separate the scalar target, and obey the adaptive likelihood inequality at the proposed budget.
body.honest_scope: Two-direction exposure identification, common class nonemptiness, coverage reduction for common observed-trajectory interval maps, the fixed-gap frontier, and the target-separating bump lemma are theorem obligations, not presumed facts. The feasibility exponent is a cited sanity reduction from PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, after the local margin bound is extended globally with \(\overline C=\max\{C_0,\delta_0^{-\alpha}\}\) and bounded rewards are translated routinely to fixed-scale Gaussian noise. The zero-exposure construction is a localized Gaussian identification diagnostic inside the Hölder--margin class, and its geometric and design conditions are local to that theorem rather than frontier assumptions. The sequential modulus and width envelope both equal \(+\infty\) when the uniformly feasible design class is empty. The exact Hölder-local rate, the number and locations of budget branches, strong duality or attainment for the semi-infinite allocation program, information saturation \(\mathcal B(w_n)\asymp n\), and sequential realization of its quotas are answer-open. At \(\rho\asymp T\), the result must reduce to fixed-design honest inference for the positive-part functional; on the fixed-gap subclass it must reduce to \(\rho^{-1/2}\); below \(T^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\), the design class is empty. Smoothness adaptation, unknown variance, more than two treatments, and anytime-valid coverage are outside the claimed frontier.
